hook: One man ate an entire airplane.
facts: His name was Michel Lotito, and he was a French entertainer.
Starting in nineteen seventy-eight, he cut a small plane into tiny pieces.
He swallowed it bit by bit, and it took him about two years.

hook: A cat was a town mayor for twenty years.
facts: The town is Talkeetna, a tiny place in Alaska.
In nineteen ninety-seven, people chose a cat called Stubbs as their honorary mayor.
He kept the job for about twenty years, until he died in twenty seventeen.

hook: Abraham Lincoln is in a wrestling hall of fame.
facts: Long before he was president, Lincoln was a strong young wrestler.
Stories say he fought around three hundred matches and lost only one.
Today he is honored in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in America.

hook: Hippos cannot swim.
facts: They are too heavy to float in the water.
Instead, they walk or bounce along the bottom of rivers.
They can hold their breath for about five minutes while they do it.

hook: The Moon is slowly running away from us.
facts: Every year it moves about four centimeters farther from Earth.
That is about as fast as your fingernails grow.
Long ago, the Moon looked much bigger in the sky than it does now.

hook: A town called Boring has two sister towns.
facts: Boring is a small town in Oregon, in the United States.
It became partners with a village in Scotland called Dull.
Later, a place in Australia joined them. Its name is Bland.

hook: Mammoths were alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
facts: Most mammoths died out about ten thousand years ago.
But a small group survived on Wrangel Island, far up in the Arctic.
They lived until about four thousand years ago, after the Great Pyramid was finished.

hook: One woman survived three huge ship disasters.
facts: Violet Jessop worked as a stewardess on big ocean ships.
In nineteen eleven, her ship Olympic crashed into a warship. The next year, she was on the Titanic.
In nineteen sixteen, her hospital ship Britannic sank too, and she survived all three.

hook: One man was hit by lightning seven times.
facts: Roy Sullivan was a park ranger in Virginia, in the United States.
Between nineteen forty-two and nineteen seventy-seven, lightning struck him seven different times.
He survived every single one, and he is in the record books for it.

hook: Your body glows in the dark.
facts: Scientists in Japan filmed people with super sensitive cameras.
Human skin gives off a very weak light that changes during the day.
It is about a thousand times too weak for our eyes to see.

hook: You cannot hum while holding your nose.
facts: When you hum with your mouth closed, the air leaves through your nose.
If you close your nose too, the air has nowhere to go.
So the sound stops almost right away. Try it now.

hook: You cannot see the Great Wall from space.
facts: Many people believe it is the only building you can see from space.
But the wall is very thin, and it is the same colour as the land around it.
Even China's first astronaut said he could not see it with his eyes.

hook: Hawaiian pizza was invented in Canada.
facts: A Greek immigrant named Sam Panopoulos ran a restaurant in Ontario.
In nineteen sixty-two, he tried putting pineapple from a can on a pizza.
He named it after the brand of the pineapple can, not after a trip to Hawaii.

hook: Caesar salad has nothing to do with Julius Caesar.
facts: It was created by Caesar Cardini, an Italian who had a restaurant in Mexico.
The story says that in nineteen twenty-four, his kitchen was almost empty.
He mixed what was left, and his own name ended up on a world famous salad.

hook: German chocolate cake is not from Germany.
facts: It is named after an American man called Samuel German.
In eighteen fifty-two, he made a sweet baking chocolate for a company in America.
A cake recipe using his chocolate became famous, and people simply dropped his name's ending.

hook: Hell really does freeze over.
facts: Hell is a small village in Norway, near the city of Trondheim.
In winter, it often gets snow and temperatures below zero.
So almost every year, people can honestly say that Hell has frozen over.

hook: Mount Everest is not the tallest mountain.
facts: Everest is the highest above the sea, at almost nine thousand meters.
But Mauna Kea in Hawaii starts deep under the ocean.
Measured from bottom to top, it is over ten thousand meters tall.

hook: It may rain diamonds on Neptune.
facts: Deep inside Neptune and Uranus there is a lot of carbon and huge pressure.
Scientists think this pressure can squeeze the carbon into diamonds.
The diamonds could then sink slowly toward the center, like rain.

hook: One planet has winds faster than sound.
facts: Neptune is the windiest planet we know.
Its winds can blow at around two thousand kilometers per hour.
That is faster than the speed of sound here on Earth.

hook: The Sun is actually white.
facts: From Earth, the Sun often looks yellow or orange.
That is because our air scatters some of its blue light away.
Seen from space, sunlight is white, a mix of all the colours.

hook: The tongue map is completely wrong.
facts: Many school books showed sweet, salty, sour and bitter in different areas of the tongue.
It came from a bad translation of a German study.
In fact, every part of your tongue can taste every flavour.

hook: Goldfish do not have three second memories.
facts: Many people believe goldfish forget everything after a few seconds.
But scientists have trained them to push levers and react to sounds for food.
Goldfish can remember these things for months.

hook: Bulls do not get angry at red.
facts: Bulls cannot really tell red apart from green.
What makes them charge is the movement of the cape.
Tests show they attack a moving cape of any colour.

hook: Ostriches do not bury their heads in sand.
facts: This is one of the most famous animal myths in the world.
Ostriches dig holes in the ground for their eggs.
They put their heads in to turn the eggs, which from far away looks like hiding.

hook: Lemmings do not really jump off cliffs.
facts: Many people believe lemmings follow each other off cliffs on purpose.
The idea became famous through a Disney nature film from nineteen fifty-eight.
The film crew is reported to have pushed the lemmings in themselves.

hook: Napoleon was not actually short.
facts: He was about one meter sixty-nine, which was normal for his time.
The confusion partly came from old French inches, which were longer than English ones.
British cartoons also loved to draw him as a tiny angry man.

hook: Einstein never failed maths.
facts: This story has been told in schools for many years.
In fact, he had mastered very difficult maths before he was fifteen.
When he saw the rumour in a newspaper, he said it was simply not true.

hook: Medieval people knew the Earth was round.
facts: Many think people in the Middle Ages believed in a flat Earth.
But scholars had known the Earth was round since ancient Greek times.
Kings were even painted holding a round ball that stood for the world.

hook: You have far more than five senses.
facts: Sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch are only the famous ones.
You also have a sense of balance, of temperature, and of pain.
You even know where your hands are with your eyes closed. That is a sense too.

hook: Dogs are not completely colour blind.
facts: Dogs can see colours, just fewer than we do.
They see blue and yellow quite well.
But red and green look almost the same to them, a bit like brown.

hook: An earthworm has five hearts.
facts: Well, sort of. It has five pairs of tubes that pump its blood.
They work like small hearts near the front of its body.
Earthworms also have no lungs, so they breathe through their skin.

hook: Male lions do almost none of the hunting.
facts: In a lion group, the females work together to hunt.
The males mostly guard the area and protect the group.
But when the food arrives, the males often eat first.

hook: An elephant cannot jump.
facts: Adult elephants are simply too heavy to leave the ground.
Their leg bones point straight down, which makes springing up very hard.
Even when they run fast, one foot always stays on the ground.

hook: Your teeth cannot heal themselves.
facts: Your skin and bones can repair damage, but tooth enamel cannot.
Enamel is the hardest thing in the human body.
But once it breaks or wears away, your body can never grow it back.

hook: A Roman emperor declared war on the sea.
facts: Ancient writers say the emperor Caligula marched his army to the coast.
Instead of fighting, he ordered the soldiers to collect seashells.
He called the shells treasure won from the sea, and took them back to Rome.

hook: A giant wave of syrup hit Boston.
facts: In nineteen nineteen, a huge tank of molasses burst in the city.
A brown wave, several meters high, rushed through the streets.
Twenty-one people died, and people say the area smelled sweet for years.

hook: A beer flood once hit London.
facts: In eighteen fourteen, a huge beer tank burst at a brewery in London.
More than a million liters of beer poured into the streets.
It knocked down walls, and eight people lost their lives.

hook: People once danced for days and could not stop.
facts: In fifteen eighteen, a woman in Strasbourg started dancing in the street.
Within weeks, dozens and then hundreds of people had joined her.
Some danced for days, and still nobody knows for sure why it happened.

hook: A con man sold the Eiffel Tower.
facts: In nineteen twenty-five, Victor Lustig told business men that Paris wanted to sell the tower.
He pretended to be a government official and sold it for scrap metal.
The buyer was too embarrassed to tell the police, so Lustig came back and tried it again.

hook: Cleopatra was not Egyptian.
facts: She ruled Egypt, but her family came from Macedonia, in Greece.
Her family had ruled Egypt for about three hundred years.
Cleopatra is said to be the first of them to learn the Egyptian language.

hook: Leonardo da Vinci wrote backwards.
facts: Most of his notes go from right to left.
To read them easily, you need to hold the page up to a mirror.
Nobody knows for sure why he did it, but he was left-handed.

hook: One president served just thirty-one days.
facts: William Henry Harrison became president of the United States in eighteen forty-one.
He gave the longest first speech ever, almost two hours long, in cold weather.
Weeks later he fell sick, and he died just one month into the job.

hook: A pig was once put on trial.
facts: In the Middle Ages, animals could be taken to court like people.
In thirteen eighty-six, in the French town of Falaise, a pig was judged for a crime.
It was found guilty, and old stories say it was dressed in human clothes.

hook: Water can boil and freeze at the same time.
facts: It happens at one special temperature and pressure.
Scientists call it the triple point.
There, water can be ice, liquid and gas all at once.

hook: Some cats are allergic to humans.
facts: It is rare, but vets have seen it happen.
The cats react to tiny bits of human skin in the air.
They can sneeze and itch, just like people who are allergic to cats.

hook: A woodpecker's tongue wraps around its skull.
facts: Its tongue is so long it cannot fit inside its beak.
So it curls around the back of its head when it is not used.
Scientists think this may also help protect its brain while it pecks.

hook: A duck's quack does echo.
facts: For years, people said a duck's quack makes no echo.
In two thousand three, scientists in England tested it in a special room.
The quack does echo. It is just quiet and hard to hear.

hook: A turtle cannot leave its shell.
facts: Cartoons show turtles walking out of their shells.
But the shell is part of the turtle's skeleton.
Its backbone and ribs are joined to it, so the shell is part of its body.

hook: Male platypuses have poison in their legs.
facts: On their back legs they have a sharp spike.
It can deliver a venom that is very painful to humans.
It is not deadly to people, but the pain can last for weeks.

hook: Rats laugh when you tickle them.
facts: Scientists tickled rats in a laboratory.
The rats made happy squeaking sounds, too high for humans to hear.
They even came back to the scientist's hand, asking for more.

hook: Saturn has a giant storm shaped like a hexagon.
facts: At Saturn's north pole there is a cloud pattern with six straight sides.
Each side is longer than the width of Earth.
Scientists still do not fully know why it keeps that shape.

hook: One sea has no coastline at all.
facts: The Sargasso Sea is in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean.
Ocean currents form its borders, not land.
It is famous for floating golden seaweed that covers huge areas.

hook: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt.
facts: Egypt has more than one hundred pyramids.
But ancient kings in Sudan built more than two hundred.
They are smaller and steeper, and far fewer people visit them.

hook: Fanta was invented because of a war.
facts: During World War Two, Coca-Cola in Germany could not get its syrup.
So in nineteen forty, the German team made a new drink from what they had.
They used leftovers from cheese and apple making, and called it Fanta.

hook: A boy invented the popsicle by accident.
facts: In nineteen oh five, eleven-year-old Frank Epperson left a drink outside with a stick in it.
It was a cold night, and by morning it had frozen solid.
Years later he sold it as the Popsicle, and the name stuck around the world.

hook: Sticky notes came from a failed glue.
facts: In nineteen sixty-eight, a scientist tried to make a very strong glue.
Instead, he made one that was weak and could be peeled off.
Years later, a colleague used it to stop bookmarks falling out of his song book.

hook: The Slinky was born from a falling spring.
facts: In nineteen forty-three, engineer Richard James was working with springs for ships.
One spring fell off a shelf and kept walking across the floor.
He turned it into a toy, and millions have been sold since.

hook: Nobody wanted to use the first shopping carts.
facts: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart in nineteen thirty-seven.
Men thought it looked weak, and women thought it looked like a baby carriage.
So he paid people to push carts around his shops until everyone copied them.

hook: You cannot breathe and swallow at the same time.
facts: Your mouth and nose both lead into your throat.
When you swallow, a small flap closes your airway.
So for a moment, your breathing always stops.

hook: Cracking your knuckles does not cause arthritis.
facts: The popping sound comes from gas bubbles in the fluid of your joints.
One doctor cracked the knuckles of only his left hand for sixty years.
In the end, neither hand had arthritis, and he won a funny science prize for it.

hook: Twenty-three people are enough to share a birthday.
facts: In a group of just twenty-three people, the chance that two share a birthday is over one half.
It sounds wrong, because a year has three hundred sixty-five days.
But you are not comparing one person with everyone. Every pair in the room counts.

hook: Oscar statues were once made of plaster.
facts: During World War Two, metal was needed for the war.
So for three years, winners got Oscars made of painted plaster.
After the war, they could trade them in for real metal ones.

hook: Mickey Mouse's first words were hot dogs.
facts: Mickey first appeared in cartoons with no words, only sounds.
In nineteen twenty-nine, he finally spoke in a short film.
His very first words were: hot dogs, hot dogs.

hook: One tennis match lasted three days.
facts: In twenty ten, John Isner and Nicolas Mahut played at Wimbledon.
The final set alone ended seventy games to sixty-eight.
The match lasted over eleven hours, spread across three days.

hook: Olympic gold medals are mostly silver.
facts: The rules say a gold medal must contain at least six grams of gold.
The rest of the medal is made of silver.
The last medals made of solid gold were given in nineteen twelve.

hook: The fastest object in sport is not a ball.
facts: It is the shuttlecock used in badminton.
A smash has been measured at over five hundred kilometers per hour.
That is faster than any tennis serve or golf shot ever recorded.

hook: In space, flames are round.
facts: On Earth, hot air rises, which pulls a flame into a pointed shape.
In space, there is no up or down for the hot air to move.
So a flame becomes a small blue ball.

hook: In space, your tears cannot fall.
facts: Without gravity, tears do not run down your face.
They build up into a ball of water over your eye.
Astronauts say it stings, and they have to wipe it off.

hook: Moon dust smells like gunpowder.
facts: Moon dust stuck to the astronauts' suits after their walks.
Back inside the lander, they could smell it.
Many of them said it smelled like burnt gunpowder.

hook: One man is buried on the Moon.
facts: Eugene Shoemaker was a scientist who studied craters and comets.
He dreamed of going to the Moon, but he never could.
In nineteen ninety-nine, a space probe carried some of his ashes there.

hook: A French cat once went to space.
facts: In nineteen sixty-three, France sent a cat called Felicette on a rocket.
She flew more than one hundred kilometers up, and came back down safely.
She is still the only cat to have gone to space.

hook: Brazil touches almost every country in South America.
facts: Brazil is so large it covers almost half of South America.
It shares a border with ten countries and territories.
Only two countries in South America do not touch it: Chile and Ecuador.

hook: The pyramids were not built by slaves.
facts: Many films show slaves building the pyramids of Egypt.
But archaeologists found the villages where the builders lived.
They were paid workers, who ate bread, meat and beer, and got medical care.
